---
title: "Inspect local remote versions"
---

Current source work: ordinary local latest/archive inspection. This command does
not upload, restore, verify artifact bytes or change configured remote definitions.
It is separate from CAS and the deferred registry design.

```bash
proj --project . remote versions --path /physical/path/to/archive --label raw-data
proj --machine --project . remote versions --path /physical/path/to/latest --label raw-data --structure latest
```

Paths relative to the command's selected project root are supported. Use physical
paths: symlinked parents, candidate directories and VERSION files are rejected.
No active project config, Git credentials or remote account are required.

Archive is the default layout: base/label/version directories. Numeric versions
sort newest first, including empty variants. The actual directory path is retained
even when version spellings differ. Multiple spellings or full/empty variants
remain visible rather than silently selecting one for restore. Unrelated names
are skipped; malformed numeric-looking version names and special candidates fail.

Latest reads the exact label entry from base/VERSION. It reports the trailing
asterisk as metadata_untrusted, plus present and empty fields. A missing target is
reported explicitly; an absent asterisk is **not proof of verified content**.
Archive results do not infer trust from metadata and return null for that field.
An absent base or VERSION yields no entries and creates nothing. Duplicate label
entries and malformed advertised versions are errors.

Use --path-append-label false only when version directories or latest contents
are directly at the supplied base. VERSION remains at that explicit base.
For latest, reading that file means the base already exists, so present is true
and empty is false: a sibling base-empty is not selected. This mode does not
infer whether the base contains data files; directory presence is not integrity.
This makes the inspected path explicit; it is not a new remote registry format.

Machine output retains protocol v1 and adds a versions query result. No byte
verification, latest-source selection, credential discovery or publication occurs.

## Download one ordinary local version

Current source work adds remote download. It is an explicit transfer, independent
of configured source selection and build publication. For archive, supply the
exact numeric directory spelling via --remote-version (for example v1.2.3-4).
For latest, omit that option: the advertised VERSION label entry is required.
A full archive directory wins over its corresponding -empty variant.

```bash
proj --project . remote download --path /physical/archive --label raw-data --remote-version v1.2.3 --destination downloaded-data
proj --project . remote download --path /physical/latest --label raw-data --structure latest --destination downloaded-data
```

The destination parent must exist. Private staging receives all source files
(including nested and hidden files) before an existing destination changes.
Matching files receive downloaded bytes; destination-only files survive by
default. --clear explicitly discards those extras only after staging succeeds.
An empty source marker preserves existing files normally, or produces an empty
destination with --clear. A marker containing entries is rejected.

Project-root/ancestor, VCS/framework-state and overlapping destinations are
rejected, along with symlinked paths and linked/special copied entries. Hard-linked
external aliases keep their bytes. Copy/selection failure preserves the existing
destination. If installation fails, restoration is attempted; a failed rollback
reports where the original directory was retained. This is not crash atomicity
or protection against concurrent writers. Post-install cleanup failure is reported
as an installed download with incomplete private-staging cleanup.

The command does not authenticate metadata, compare downloaded bytes to CSV,
choose configured restore sources or change local VERSION/manifest/configuration.
A latest untrusted marker does not prevent this explicitly requested download;
it remains a warning about metadata, not a verified-content claim.
Machine mode returns completed: true only after successful completion.

Permission flags are preserved for newly downloaded entries. Merge mode retains
existing file/directory permission flags, and an existing destination root keeps
its flags even with --clear. Ownership, ACLs and extended attributes are outside
this bounded guarantee; replacing a tree is not a full metadata-preserving backup.

## Inspect and apply a concrete local file policy

Current source work adds remote store for file-inspected transfers to one
explicit physical target. This is the file-policy layer, not configured build
publication or archive/version metadata management. Supply --inspect file
explicitly; manifest/none inspection are not accepted by this bounded command.
The existing configuration default inspection is unchanged.

```bash
proj --machine --project . remote store --source generated --destination /physical/remote/output/v1.2.3 --inspect file --dry-run
proj --project . remote store --source generated --destination /physical/remote/output/v1.2.3 --inspect file --strategy sync-diff
```

The default strategy is sync-diff, matching projr. upload-all selects every
source file and keeps destination-only files; upload-missing uploads only absent
names; sync-diff uploads new/different files and removes destination-only files;
sync-purge lists all existing files for removal and every source file for upload.
A dry run reports uploads, overwrites, removals and same_bytes (informational
even when those paths are re-uploaded). It creates nothing.

This command uses current streaming MD5 byte inventories, not modification time
or a claim of authenticity. Hidden/nested files are included; empty subdirectories
are not transfer records. The destination parent must exist. It stages selected
source bytes, checks their hashes and rechecks source/target inventories before
the shared guarded installer changes the target. Mirror execution builds a full
replacement snapshot, so unchanged bytes may be copied privately too; do not
interpret the plan as a syscall or disk-I/O count.

Source files stay unchanged. Retained paths of the same type keep existing
permission flags; new paths use source flags. The download safeguards and limits
above apply, including Windows read-only cleanup failures and partial cleanup
residue. No crash/concurrent-writer isolation or ACL/ownership/xattr parity follows.

VERSION, manifest.csv, configured remotes, cue selection, historical comparison,
empty remote naming and GitHub/CAS structures are untouched. Use the concrete
version directory as destination; this command does not publish a complete
discoverable remote snapshot by itself.

Native filename aliases (for example A.csv/a.csv on a case-insensitive target)
are rejected before staging when the planned spelling differs from an existing
entry. This includes directory components and keeps upload-missing from becoming
an overwrite. Case-sensitive targets retain distinct names. Case-only migrations
are not silently inferred by this bounded file-policy command.


## Work with explicit GitHub Release assets

The source CLI provides remote github assets, remote github upload and remote
github download. Each requires --repository owner/repo and --tag RELEASE_TAG.
Upload also requires --source FILE and --name ASSET_NAME; --create-release
explicitly permits a missing Release to be created. Existing names are rejected
without deletion. Download requires --name, --destination FILE and --max-bytes N.
Source/destination file paths are relative to the selected project root unless
absolute. The destination parent must already exist.

Use an existing GITHUB_PAT, GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN, in that order. Public list
and download requests can be anonymous. GITHUB_API_URL supports an explicit
Enterprise API endpoint including /api/v3. Tokens are never command arguments.
No authentication setup or additional credential helper is installed.

Machine assets returns result.assets; machine upload/download returns completed
through the existing worker. ZIP creation/extraction, projr metadata ZIP handling
and configured restore are not yet provided by these explicit asset commands.
An interrupted upload can have an uncertain remote result: inspect before retry.
Downloads stage complete bytes before replacement, preserve existing permissions,
and reject protected project state, links and special files. No archive integrity,
crash atomicity or concurrent-writer isolation claim follows.

The CLI does not initialise HTTP wire logging and its own error messages omit
tokens, response bodies and signed redirect URLs. Library embedders must avoid
ureq DEBUG/TRACE logging for sensitive requests because dependency logging is
not redacted. Redirects remove Authorization but do not confine network access
to a provider host; this transport is not a network sandbox.


## GitHub ZIP packaging and explicit directory transfer candidate

This candidate extends the native Release transport with projr flat names:
prefix-label-vVERSION.zip for archive, prefix-label.zip for latest, and
-empty before .zip for empty variants. With no prefix, the label is always
used, including path_append_label=false. Metadata assets remain shared and
unprefixed: manifest.zip contains manifest.csv, VERSION.zip contains VERSION,
and CHANGELOG.zip contains CHANGELOG.md. Directory ZIP entries are relative to
the selected source, without an enclosing folder. Nonempty parent-directory entries retain Unix
permission modes; empty directory entries remain omitted. Empty sources contain the
single zero-byte projr-empty sentinel; empty subdirectories are not archived.

The CLI adds remote github upload-directory (label/structure/remote-version,
optional prefix/path-append-label), upload-metadata (kind manifest/version/
changelog and a source directory), and download-directory (exact asset name,
destination, max-bytes, max-expanded-bytes, optional clear/empty). Uploads remain
new-name-only; metadata is packaged byte-for-byte rather than silently merged.
Download stages extraction privately and uses the existing guarded merge/clear
installer. Explicit empty requires exactly the sentinel and consumes it before
installation. Destination-only files survive unless clear is requested.

Safety changes from R's direct utils::unzip: bounded expanded bytes and100000
members, CRC validation, reject links/special/encrypted entries, traversal,
backslashes, device names, native aliases, duplicate members and parent/file
collisions before project installation. Retain existing installer rollback and
Windows backup-cleanup limits; no crash/concurrent-writer guarantee is added.

Ponytail full: one ZIP crate with only Deflate enabled, existing MD5 inventory,
HTTP client and guarded installer. No backend interface, registry or new YAML
policy. Independent tests cover exact metadata/Unicode/hidden/empty members,
malicious names, CRC/expanded limits and mocked actual ZIP upload/download
merge/clear. No local heavy tests; remote lock resolution, exact-head platform/
pinned/docs acceptance and independent review are pending.

Pinned sources:
[flat names](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/90be50132d16aee33e39c0f7f35ef906c35f5397/R/remote.R#L525),
[ZIP layout](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/90be50132d16aee33e39c0f7f35ef906c35f5397/R/misc.R#L638),
[empty sentinel](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/90be50132d16aee33e39c0f7f35ef906c35f5397/R/remote-github.R#L350),
[metadata assets](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/90be50132d16aee33e39c0f7f35ef906c35f5397/R/remote-versions.R#L1).
Configured source selection/restore, historical metadata merging, latest asset
replacement, credentials-helper fallback and CAS remain outstanding. This
source candidate does not update the published/installed preview.

Review amendments share the existing native directory-entry alias guard with
file-policy transfers, validate empty-directory CRC with a bounded probe, and
never persist an expanded-byte probe beyond each member's advertised size.
Directory modes apply deepest-first after extraction; an existing destination's
modes still follow the previously documented merge policy. File-only ZIPs from
other writers have no directory privacy metadata to restore. Source root modes
are not encoded as a new manifest field. No ACL/ownership/xattr claim follows.
Temporary paths are created beneath the physical canonical system temp directory;
macOS /var aliases are not an excuse to weaken external path guards.

Extraction also checks actual directory spelling immediately after creation,
rejecting filesystems that rewrite it rather than merging distinct Unicode
members. The extracted-tree owner restores directory owner access for cleanup;
explicit close reports a retained path on cleanup failure. The directory-transfer
command checks extraction and transfer cleanup on success and failure and
distinguishes installed output from failed transfer. Readonly/zero-mode owned
directory cleanup is exercised unprivileged in the pinned gate.


## Configured single-label restore candidate

remote restore --label LABEL --max-bytes N --max-expanded-bytes N resolves
one declared final directory from merged active configuration. Optional
--position source/dest, --provider local/github and --title restrict lookup;
--profile follows existing earlier-profile/local precedence. --remote-version
selects an exact archive version; otherwise numeric newest is selected. GitHub
latest reads canonical VERSION.zip, then downloads its label ZIP. --repository
owner/repo avoids requiring Git; otherwise origin is inspected locally and its
host must match the API. GITHUB_API_URL and existing environment tokens retain
the explicit transport contract. No credentials are installed.

Existing per-directory source.local/source.github title references or named
inline definitions precede eligible build.local/build.github destinations.
A shared referenced definition may be refined inline through the existing deep
merge (null still inherits). Destination source:false excludes it; true or a
matching label preference beats the first eligible fallback. content:null/false
selects nothing, true selects declared non-cache roles, and lists select declared
labels. Source/provider/title declaration order is preserved. No retry switches
to another configured source after lookup/download fails.

A valid root manifest.csv is required, matching projr's prior-build gate.
Labels with no recorded files and advertised empty variants skip without clearing.
CSV history is not used as an integrity/trust proof. Full sources stage before
the existing merge/clear installer; --clear never removes files before a source
has been found and copied. Default merge preserves destination-only files.
Machine results disclose restored/skipped, selected provider/title/version and
destination; failures stay structured and do not print tokens or raw config.

This deliberately fixes R source-selection indexing/inline-definition bugs and
clear-before-lookup data loss. It does not add R's implicit hard-coded archive
fallback: undeclared remotes/paths are errors under the agreed explicit mapping
contract. Nonempty get policy mappings fail explicitly rather than pretending
that R's ineffective get.strategy/get.conflict controls work. Send policy is not
executed by restore. Definitions retain local path versus GitHub title/tag id
semantics, including spaces and @version tag normalization.

Boundary: ordinary inline remote/source fields are accepted by this command's
read-only configuration projection only. Normal build validation still rejects
unsupported ordinary publication fields, preventing silently ignored uploads.
Configured automatic publication, cue/history policy integration, all-label
default restore, complete credential-helper fallback and the issue706 registry
remain subsequent work. Installed preview remains unchanged.

Pinned comparison:
[restore gate/selection/download](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/90be50132d16aee33e39c0f7f35ef906c35f5397/R/restore.R#L140),
[inline destination defaults](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/90be50132d16aee33e39c0f7f35ef906c35f5397/R/yml-dest.R#L197),
[content eligibility](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/90be50132d16aee33e39c0f7f35ef906c35f5397/R/dest-send.R#L416).
Ponytail full reuses merged YAML, typed core validation, CSV decoding, numeric
version comparison and guarded local/ZIP installers. No backend trait, new
registry or persistence schema. Filesystem and mocked REST actual CLI fixtures
cover source priority, references/inline/profiles, destination preference,
numeric archives, VERSION ZIP latest, clear/merge/empty and corrupt failure
preservation. No actual GitHub Release mutation or local heavy test is performed.
Exact-head remote verification and independent review are pending.
